title: Count Vowels and Consonants
statement: Given a string word, return how many vowels and consonants it contains. Ignore case and ignore non-letter characters.
think: What is the task asking? Count letters in two groups: vowels and consonants.
What is the key operation? Check each character and decide which group it belongs to.
What wording signals stand out? Count, vowels, consonants.
What is the brute force idea? Scan the string once for vowels and once for consonants.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use one pass with two counters.
What are the edge cases? Spaces, punctuation, uppercase letters.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(1) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I iterate once, ignore non-letters, and update either the vowel or consonant counter.
interview: I would use a single pass through the string. For each letter, I check whether it is a vowel and update one of two counters.
ru: Это задача на один проход. Мы просто делим буквы на две категории и считаем обе сразу.

nice: Do not mention that one pass is enough

gaps: Important: be confident with simple character classification
Nice to have: explain why this is O(1) space
constraints: Assume the input is a short word or phrase.
whyThisPattern: This is a Linear Scan problem because we only need one pass and simple per-character classification.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because we do not need per-letter frequencies.
Not Two Pointers, because there is no compare-from-both-ends behavior.
